questions.q: What is an "invariant" in the context of Foundry testing?
options: A variable that never changes value during compilation
A property that must hold true no matter what sequence of calls happens
A function that can only be called once
A gas optimization applied automatically by the compiler
questions.explain: An invariant is a property — like solvency — that has to remain true across any sequence of calls, not just a single happy-path call.

questions.q: What does `targetContract()` do in an invariant test?
options: Deploys the contract to mainnet
Tells Forge which contract's public functions to generate a random call sequence against
Marks a contract as immutable
Deletes the contract after the test
questions.explain: targetContract() designates which contract Forge fuzzes a sequence of calls against, checking the invariant after each call.

questions.q: Why do real invariant suites typically fuzz a handler contract instead of the target contract's raw public functions?
options: Handlers are required by the Solidity compiler
A handler constrains inputs to realistic ranges and tracks ghost state, instead of wasting runs on unconstrained calls
Handlers make the contract immutable
Fuzzing raw functions is not supported by Forge
questions.explain: Fuzzing raw functions directly wastes most of a run on calls with no realistic bounds — a handler wraps them with bound() constraints and ghost-variable tracking.

options: A private state variable hidden from Etherscan
Off-chain tracking state a handler keeps purely to verify an invariant, not part of the real contract
A variable that only exists during a fuzz test's setUp()
A deprecated Solidity keyword
questions.explain: Ghost variables like ghost_depositSum track cumulative totals the handler records, letting the invariant check the real contract's state against what was actually sent.

questions.q: When an invariant test fails, what does Forge give you to help debug it?
options: Nothing — you have to re-run the entire suite with verbose logging
The exact call sequence that broke the invariant, so the failure can be reproduced deterministically
A gas report for the failing call only
An automatic patch suggestion for the contract
questions.explain: Forge prints the specific sequence of calls that triggered the invariant failure, avoiding a guessing game over which of hundreds of random calls caused it.
